## FINDING 1 — AGENT HOOKS  (reported HIGH/AISPM 2026-08-26)
Doc ms.date 2026-08-07, updated_at 2026-08-25.
Implements the FRAMEWORK-NEUTRAL **AGENT-HOOKS-0.1** contract:
  github.com/responsibleai/agent-hooks/blob/main/spec/AGENT-HOOKS-0.1.md
"so policy engines, approval gateways, budget guards, content filters, and egress controls can target
one common control surface." CONTROL PLANE, NOT TELEMETRY PLANE — every interceptor returns a verdict.

EIGHT INTERCEPTION POINTS (transform target in parens):
  agent_startup   (not transformable)
  input           (input content + role)
  pre_model_call  (messages sent to the model)
  post_model_call (response content, framework-executed tool calls, finish reason)
  pre_tool_call   (tool arguments)
  post_tool_call  (tool result)
  output          (final response content)
  agent_shutdown  (not transformable)
Typical tool run: agent_startup -> input -> pre_model_call -> post_model_call -> pre_tool_call ->
                  post_tool_call -> pre_model_call -> post_model_call -> output -> agent_shutdown

VERDICTS: allow | warn | deny | **escalate** (liftable deny resolved via approval `resolver`;
          WITHOUT a resolver the deny simply stands) | transform (rewrite at a `$target` path)

RUNTIME GUARANTEES: fail closed (invalid contexts/verdicts, interceptor failures AND enforcement
  failures all block); transform write-back (unappliable transform fails the run); BUFFERED STREAMING
  (nothing reaches caller until the full response passes post_model_call + output);
  verdict-gated persistence; complete bundle installation (agent+chat+function install as ONE unit).

*** THE FOUR DOCUMENTED BYPASSES — THE MOST VALUABLE PART ***
1. HOSTED TOOLS: "Tools executed by a model provider don't pass through Agent Framework's
   function-invocation seam." They surface at post_model_call, but pre_tool_call / post_tool_call
   "can't block the provider's server-side execution."
   => an agent on provider-hosted tools has NO enforceable tool gate, only after-the-fact visibility.
2. ORDERING: "Middleware placed before the bundle is outside the enforcement boundary. Treat outer
   position as outer trust." Coverage depends on ORDER, not presence.
3. COOPERATIVE BOUNDARY: interceptors run in the host process, receive full content, are NOT
   sandboxed. "Only register interceptors you trust." "Code paths that bypass the guarded agent
   pipeline aren't covered."
4. PERSISTENCE: with require_per_service_call_history_persistence=True each model exchange persists
   once its post_model_call verdict permits — "a later `output` deny doesn't roll back that already
   permitted history." An output-only egress policy leaves model content DURABLE.

CONFIG (create_agent_hooks_middleware): interceptors (>=1) | resolver | **mode: enforce |
  evaluate_only** | composition (default sequential `first_deny`) | identity_provider (default
  jcs-sha256) | timeout (default 5 s; a SYNC interceptor blocking the event loop can't be preempted) |
  record_sink.
*** evaluate_only IS A FALSE-ASSURANCE STATE: runs every interceptor, records every verdict, ALLOWS
    EVERY ACTION. MS: "Don't describe an evaluate_only deployment as enforced governance." ***
RULES: exactly ONE bundle per agent (stacked bundles rejected); bundle can't be split; install on
  Agent (not on a chat client / context provider); each nested agent needs its OWN bundle.
record_sink yields InterceptionRecord = decision, reason, interceptor summary, mode, identity,
  sequence — **PAYLOAD-FREE** (high signal, low sensitivity; but you can't reconstruct WHAT was
  blocked from the record). Default one Agent Hooks session per run;
  create_agent_hooks_middleware_from_emitter() spans multiple runs under one session/approval ledger.
AVAILABILITY: **PYTHON ONLY, EXPERIMENTAL** (ExperimentalWarning on first use).
  .NET and Go are told to use plain middleware + tool approval + Agent Safety instead
  => within one fleet the same nominal control exists on some agents and not others.
Install: pip install "agent-framework-core[agent-hooks]" — deliberately NOT in [all].
GOTCHA: for tools with approval_mode="always_require", the framework builds the human approval request
  BEFORE function middleware runs, so a pre_tool_call transform changes arguments AFTER the user
  approved the originals. MS says transform at post_model_call or escalate at pre_tool_call instead.

## FINDING 2 — FIDES  (reported HIGH/AIRT 2026-08-26; COVERAGE-GAP RECOVERY)
Flow Integrity Deterministic Enforcement System. Doc ms.date **2026-06-23**, updated_at 2026-08-25.
Based on the FIDES paper (Costa et al., arxiv.org/abs/2505.23643). Ships in agent-framework-core
behind `agent_framework.security`. EXPERIMENTAL, **PYTHON ONLY**.
MS's framing: defensive prompts "are heuristic… they don't make the next attack impossible";
sanitization "is lossy"; "pre/post-hoc monitoring detects damage; it doesn't prevent it."

TWO-AXIS LABEL on every Content item (`security_label` in additional_properties):
  integrity:        trusted | untrusted
  confidentiality:  public | private | user_identity
  combine_labels() = MOST RESTRICTIVE WINS (untrusted > trusted; user_identity > private > public)
FOUR PARTS: ContentLabel (data) | LabelTrackingFunctionMiddleware (propagates) |
  PolicyEnforcementFunctionMiddleware (checks BEFORE the tool runs) |
  quarantined_llm + ContentVariableStore (process untrusted content safely)

SINK ANNOTATIONS (the enforcement primitive):
  accepts_untrusted: False        -> refuse the tool whenever ANY untrusted content is in scope
                                    (intended for file writes, destructive ops, production mutation)
  max_allowed_confidentiality    -> cap what a sink may leak (`public` for anything that publishes
                                    externally: comments, tweets, public webhooks)
SOURCE ANNOTATIONS: per-item security_label (preferred) > tool-level source_integrity >
  implicit propagation from input labels (right default for pure transformation tools).

SecureAgentConfig (a CONTEXT PROVIDER) — the posture surface:
  auto_hide_untrusted        default **True**  -> untrusted results never reach the main model; they
                                                 go to the ContentVariableStore and the context gets a
                                                 **var_<id>** VariableReferenceContent
  default_integrity          default UNTRUSTED (secure-by-default; **flipping to TRUSTED silently
                                                relabels every unannotated tool's output as safe**)
  default_confidentiality    default PUBLIC
  allow_untrusted_tools      explicit per-tool EXEMPTION list (data fetchers must be callable in any
                             context; security tools auto-allowed)
  block_on_violation         default True
  approval_on_violation      default False -> when True the control collapses to user click-through
  enable_audit_log           default True
  enable_policy_enforcement  default True; **False = DRY RUN: labels propagate, audit log fills,
                             NO SINK IS EVER BLOCKED** (governance telemetry, zero enforcement)
  quarantine_chat_client     without it quarantined_llm returns placeholders
THREE MODES: hard block | human-in-the-loop (approval_on_violation) | dry run (enforcement off).
quarantined_llm(prompt, variable_ids=[...]) — isolated context, **NO TOOLS ATTACHED**, result itself
  labeled untrusted and re-entered into the store. So embedded "call write_file" is only TEXT.

DOCUMENTED LIMITATIONS = coverage map:
  1. Labels are OPT-IN PER DATA SOURCE — a forgotten tool falls back to defaults.
  2. Most-restrictive propagation is CONSERVATIVE — once untrusted enters, the run stays untrusted
     "unless you explicitly drop it" (the DROP is where a bypass would live).
  3. Approvals are COARSE — the label algebra is not shown to the approving user.
  4. quarantined_llm is SINGLE-TURN and TOOLS-FREE; multi-turn quarantined sub-agents unsupported.

## ADJACENT (read, not reported)
- Agent middleware (3 types: agent run / function calling / IChatClient-or-chat). Termination via
  MiddlewareTermination or simply not calling call_next. Result override in streaming AND
  non-streaming. Middleware doc ms.date 2026-08-07, updated_at 2026-08-25.
- Tool approval (approval_mode="always_require"), Agent Safety (heuristic best practices).
- Go SDK: middleware only; built-ins are toolautocall, structured output, otelprovider, run logger.
